- If sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.  
- When sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per sentiment shift.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in first 5–7 days, assume momentum bias; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5 days), apply +1–2% upward bias to first 3–5 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., negative → positive → negative), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% in mid-horizon.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after spike, model fails to correct; apply downward correction of 1–3% for next 3–5 days after peak.
